exam-results-day: Results are now published in three stages (morning, noon, evening) instead of at once. How do your numbers and your design change?
cricket-scores: Fans want ball-by-ball audio commentary as well as the score. What new bottleneck appears, and how would you size it?
course-registration: The university wants first-years to get first pick. How would you run a fair, priority-based queue at 9:00 without the portal falling over?
election-night: Readers want a personal page that only tracks the five seats they care about. Can you still serve it from prebuilt files?
breaking-news: A correction must replace a wrong headline everywhere within 30 seconds. Which caches and edges do you purge, and in what order?
recipe-blog: Readers can now rate recipes and see the average. Where does that number live, and how stale is it allowed to be?
docs-site: The docs must work fully offline for engineers on a submarine. What changes in how you build and ship them?
festival-grocery: Delivery slots are limited and everyone wants 6–8 pm on festival eve. How do you hand out slots fairly at peak?
game-launch: The game adds a global leaderboard updated after every match. How do you keep it fast for two million new players?
coding-contest: A problem statement has a typo found at 8:03. How do you publish the fix to everyone mid-contest?
exam-results-scaled: A second exam board publishes results on the same morning. Share the infrastructure or keep it separate? Defend your choice.
hospital-appointments: Doctors can now run late, pushing every later slot. How do you update thousands of bookings and tell patients?
library-catalogue: Members want "notify me when this book is back". How would you add holds and fair notifications?
bank-ledger: Regulators ask for the balance of every account at exactly midnight last March. How does your design answer that?
train-booking: Tatkal tickets open at 10:00 and sell out in a minute. What would you change to make it fair against bots?
warehouse-inventory: A shopper wants items from three warehouses in one parcel. How do you reserve stock across shards safely?
photo-backup: Users want "find photos of my dog" by searching pictures, not file names. What new pieces does that need?
saas-tenants: A giant customer demands its data stay in its own country. How do you place and route that tenant?
chat-history: Users can now edit and delete messages. How does that work with an append-friendly storage engine?
iot-sensors: Engineers want an alert within 2 seconds when vibration spikes. Where does that check run: at ingest, in a stream, or in the database?
kv-store: Your key–value store must support a range scan (all keys from A to F). What does that do to consistent hashing?
ride-locations: Riders want to see every nearby car moving smoothly in real time. How often do you send updates, and to whom?
live-auction: The auction adds automatic "bid up to my maximum" proxy bids. How do you process them without races?
whiteboard: Two students erase and redraw the same shape at the same moment while one is offline. Whose change wins, and how?
multiplayer-quiz: A player's phone drops mid-question and reconnects 3 seconds later. Can they still answer? What's fair?
push-notifications: Marketing wants to send at 9 am in each user's own time zone. How do you schedule 30 million sends?
order-webhooks: A merchant asks for events in exact order per order (paid before shipped). How do you guarantee that with retries?
support-tickets: The airline wants an AI assistant to draft replies before agents see tickets. Where does it fit, and how do you keep it from slowing the queue?
food-orders: Restaurants can now pause orders when the kitchen is overloaded. How do you reflect that instantly in the app?
course-videos: Learners want to download whole courses to watch on a flight. What changes for storage, rights and the CDN?
status-page: Your status page provider has an outage at the same time as your service. How do customers still learn what's going on?
public-api: A partner wants a bulk export of a million records. Do you raise their rate limit or design something else?
sms-otp: SMS costs triple in one country overnight. How do you cut costs without hurting sign-in success?
login-attack: Attackers move from guessing passwords to stealing session cookies. What do you watch and change next?
payments: A payment succeeds at the bank but your service crashes before recording it. Walk through how you find and fix it.
clickstream: Product managers want dashboards updated every second instead of every hour. What would you add, and what would it cost?
travel-saga: The airline's cancel API is down while you need to compensate. What does the saga do, and what does the customer see?
fraud-detection: Fraudsters learn your rules and adapt within a day. How do you retrain and roll out a new model safely?
recommendations: Readers complain they only ever see the same kind of book. How would you add variety without hurting clicks?
monolith-split: Two services both need the customer's address. Who owns it, and how does the other stay up to date?
marketplace-checkout: A seller's stock count is wrong after a flash sale. How do you find where the numbers drifted?
health-records: A doctor needs emergency access to a record they normally can't see. How do you allow it and audit it?
file-sharing: A client wants a link that works only five times. Where do you count downloads when files come from a CDN?
password-manager: A family wants to share a few passwords while each keeps a private vault. How do keys and encryption change?
api-keys: Developers want short-lived tokens instead of long-lived keys in mobile apps. How would you issue them?
school-sso: A teacher leaves mid-term. How do you remove their access everywhere within minutes, including apps that cache sessions?
zero-downtime-migration: Halfway through the backfill, you find a bug that split names wrongly. How do you recover without downtime?
daily-deploys: A deploy is safe for the app but changes the database. How does your canary catch problems the database causes?
algoverse-capstone: AlgoVerse adds live classes with a teacher and 500 learners. Which new pieces would you add first, and why?
video-platform: Creators want live streaming, not just uploads. What changes in ingest, processing and delivery?
cyclone-warning: The mobile network fails completely in two districts but SMS still works. How do you get warnings to people there?
podcast-hit: The host wants to show creators exact download counts per episode. How do you count downloads that the CDN serves?
product-catalogue: Shoppers want to filter by any combination of 30 attributes. When do you stop adding indexes and add a search engine instead?
game-leaderboard: The game adds friends-only leaderboards. Where do you compute "my rank among my 200 friends" quickly?
feature-flags: A flag targets "users who joined in the last 30 days in India". Where is that rule evaluated, and with what data?
stock-ticker: Users want an alert when a share crosses a price they choose. How do you check a million alerts on every tick?
report-exports: A huge export takes 40 minutes and a worker dies at minute 35. How do you avoid starting over?
multi-region-reads: A customer in Europe wants to book while Mumbai is unreachable but not yet declared down. What does the site do?
order-fulfilment: The same OrderPacked event is delivered twice and the courier gets booked twice. Where do you add the protection?
exam-proctoring: Ten thousand flags arrive in an hour but you have 50 reviewers. How do you prioritise what humans look at?
banking-sessions: The customer gets a new phone. How do they move their session safely without visiting a branch?
mobile-old-versions: A security bug is found in an app version used by 8% of customers. How quickly can you force an update, and what breaks?
messaging-app: Users want to search their chat history, but the server can't read messages. Where does search run, and how?
tax-deadline: The government extends the deadline by a week at 11 pm on the last night. What happens to your load, and what would you change?
webinar-signup: The organiser wants a waiting list once seats run out, with automatic promotion when someone cancels. How would you build it?
job-scheduler: A job must run at 9 am in each customer's own time zone, for 12,000 customers. How do you schedule and spread that work?
shopping-list: Two people rename the same item at the same time while offline. Latest wins loses one name. Can you do better?
legal-documents: A court orders one document deleted, but your storage is write-once for closed cases. How do you comply?
newsletter: Readers in 40 time zones want the newsletter at 7 am their time. How do you change the send plan?
search-dependency: Pricing is fine but the search index itself becomes slow. What can search show then, and how do you decide?
oncall-alerts: A new team joins with 200 old alert rules they swear are all important. How do you migrate them to the new approach?
service-mesh: One team needs a 2-second timeout but the platform default is 300 ms. How do you allow exceptions without losing consistency?
data-warehouse: Finance now wants sales numbers updated every 15 minutes instead of nightly. What parts of the design change?
admin-roles: A customer wants a custom role: can edit employees in one department only. How do you model that?
risky-launch: The new pricing is better on average but worse for 3% of customers. How do you decide whether to launch, and what do you tell them?
maps-navigation: A road closes for a festival with one day's notice. How does that change reach routing, tiles and arrival times?
photo-contest: Entrants want to see their photo's live vote count during voting day. What does that add to your numbers?
restaurant-reviews: The site adds "sort reviews by most helpful", with votes on each review. How do you keep cached pages fresh without rebuilding constantly?
hotel-rooms: A hotel also sells rooms through two other websites. How do you avoid selling the last room three times?
nearby-search: Users want results along their driving route, not around one point. How does the cell approach change?
ride-trip: The rider cancels at the same moment the driver taps "Arrived". Which wins, and how does the state machine decide?
mobile-gateway: The web app and a smartwatch app want their own home screens too. One gateway for all, or one per app? Why?
streaming-outage: The stadium's own internet link fails instead of a cloud region. What can still keep viewers watching?
tax-service: The provider changes its prices to charge per cart line instead of per call. How would you redesign caching and batching?
search-indexing: Recruiters want saved searches that alert them when a matching job appears. Where do you run those matches?
notification-prefs: A customer says they got a marketing SMS an hour after opting out. How do you find out which sender ignored the change, and why?
upload-scanning: A customer must share a 5 GB database dump to reproduce a bug. Your scanners time out on files that big. What do you do?
dr-drill: The drill showed scaling servers took 14 minutes. Give three ways to get the recovery time under 10 minutes, and what each costs.
social-network: The network adds short videos to the feed. Which parts of the design change most, and which stay the same?
marathon-tracking: Families now want a live dot moving along the course map between mats. Where does the position come from, and what does it cost?
username-signup: Users may change their username once a year, and old names are held for 30 days. How do you store and release held names?
loyalty-points: Points now expire 12 months after they were earned, oldest first. How do you compute and show expiring points without scanning every ledger row?
autocomplete: Suggestions should become personal, favouring things each shopper bought before. What changes about caching, and where do you merge?
parcel-tracking: Customers want a live van position on a map for the last 30 minutes of delivery. What do you add, and how often do vans report?
live-comments: The organisers want to remove abusive comments within two seconds, before most viewers see them. Where in the flow would you check?
partner-api-limits: A second airline allows 200 calls a second but charges per call. How would your caching and limits differ between the two airlines?
cache-stampede: The homepage becomes personal: each reader sees their own topics. Which of the stampede protections still apply, and what new risk appears?
loan-application: Regulators require that a declined customer can see exactly which check declined them and why. What do you store, and for how long?
ad-clicks: An advertiser disputes their invoice, saying a competitor clicked their ads all month. What data do you keep to settle it?
secrets-vault: The secrets store itself goes down for 20 minutes. Which services keep working, and how would you design for that?
load-test: You can't afford a full-size copy of production for testing. How would you load-test safely against production itself?
ticketing-platform: The artist wants resale capped at face value, with resold tickets re-issued to the new fan. How does that change the design?
